title: The persistence of handwriting
summary_es: Por qué la escritura a mano no desaparece. Prefijos pre-, un-, omni- y cambios de raíz.
text: Predictions of the death of handwriting have proved remarkably {{1}}. Although most adults now type far more than they write, the pen has shown a stubborn {{2}} to disappear. Part of the explanation is practical: notes taken by hand appear to be more {{3}} retained than those typed, presumably because the slower pace forces the writer to summarise rather than transcribe. But there is also something less {{4}} at work. A handwritten letter carries an {{5}} of the person who wrote it that no typeface can reproduce, and it is this {{6}} that makes such letters so hard to throw away. Whether the habit will survive another generation of {{7}} screens is uncertain. For now, at least, reports of its {{8}} remain exaggerated.

gaps.explanation_es: Las predicciones se adelantaron: pre- + mature = prematuro. «Immature» sería inmaduro, que no encaja.
Tras el adjetivo «stubborn» va un nombre, y con sentido negativo: un- + willing + -ness.
Adverbio que modifica al participio «retained»: readily = con facilidad. La y pasa a i.
«Something less definable» = algo menos fácil de definir. Verbo + -able (se pierde la e).
«Carry an imprint of» = llevar la huella de. El artículo «an» ya indica que empieza por vocal.
Tras «this» va un nombre: intimate → intimacy.
Las pantallas están en todas partes: omni- (todo) + present.
Tras el posesivo «its» va un nombre: extinct → extinction.
